name: Reflective STN, Nintendo DMG-01 (Retro Display Lab reconstruction)

attribution.changes: Values copied into one JSON profile. The contrast tables (stn.target_q, drift_per_frame, optical, anchors, corrections) are recomputed by tools/dmg01_wheel.mjs with the source's own solver at every 0.01 of the wheel from 0.85 to 1.08, with the optical calibration continued beyond the nominal shades. Used without the pixel aperture, the passive-matrix crosstalk and the row-latch scan-out, which belong to the 160x144 dot grid.

panel.ref: Nintendo Game Boy technical data (DMG-DIMENSIONS-01); DMG drive record dmg-drive-v1.json

palette.interpolation: linear light, piecewise between the five states
palette.ref: BGB, The reality of DMG colors (DMG-COLOR-01): central-patch samples

drive.mapping: shade = floor(3 (1 - luma) + 0.5), luma = Rec.709 weights on the encoded sRGB value (Retro Display Lab gameboy_drive_index)
drive.note: inferred from LD0/LD1 plus four CPG pulses per line; exact LH5077 switching truth table unavailable

contrast.note: 30 kohm potentiometer between ground and the approximately -19 V LCD rail, with its wiper feeding IR3E02 VR
contrast.range: x0.85 to x1.08: a repairer measured -11 V and -14 V at the ends of a real DMG wheel against -13 V for good contrast (chipmusic.org, "DMG screen stuck on max contrast?", 2015): one board. The source supports 0.88 to 1.08.
contrast.solved: every 0.01 by tools/dmg01_wheel.mjs with the source's solver; the source tabulates 0.88, 1.00 and 1.08 only

stn.layout: drift_per_frame[(condition*4 + shade)*bins + bin], bin over director coordinate q in [0, 1]
stn.method: overdamped 1D Frank-Oseen/Ericksen-Leslie reduction with finite anchoring; 15-wavelength sliced Jones round trip through two polarizers and reflector
stn.claim: No parameter is presented as a measurement of an unaged DMG-LCD-01 or DMG-LCD-06 cell. Unknown analogue levels, material identity, and polarizer spectra remain bounded reconstructions.
stn.optical_range: optical states continue below 0.25 (lighter than nominal white) and above 1 (darker than nominal black), linearly in luminance

temperature.law: drift per frame scaled by exp(activation_K (1/293.15 - 1/T))

retention.ref: Nakazono et al. (Merck Japan, 1994) sticking-voltage regression; the optical gain is an explicit bridge (Retro Display Lab)

shadow.ref: Retro Display Lab reflector shadow (DMG-APERTURE-01), reference-image matched

geometry.note: DMG glass thickness not published; same front stack as the TN profiles (assumed)

limitations: The target is a healthy period-DMG appearance reconstructed from DMG-specific evidence and contemporary STN measurements, not a surviving aged specimen
No identified original panel analogue waveform, fill material, or full voltage-transmission curve; these remain bounded literature reconstructions
Response varies with specimen, temperature, contrast wheel, and aging

LH5076/LH5077 analogue output resistance and the DMG electrode mask remain unavailable; WS5 propagates comparable period-driver, ITO, cell-gap, and dielectric ranges rather than claiming a measured Nintendo coefficient
